algorithm.title: Mild Elevations of Serum ALT and AST: Diagnosis.

cell.label: Elevated ALT and AST less than 5 times normal
History and physical examination. Discontinue hepatotoxic medications and alcohol.
Consider repeat ALT/AST or a clarifying test to confirm abnormality.
Liver chemistries, PT, albumin, CBC with platelets, Hepatitis A, B, and C serologies, serum iron, total iron binding capacity, ferritin, glucose or hemoglobin A1C, and abdominal ultrasound.
Proceed with directed evaluation and treatment.
Symptomatic or evidence of hepatic decompensation?
Expedited evaluation.
Lifestyle modification: Discontinue alcohol. Stop hepatotoxic medications. Weight loss. Diabetes control.
Six-month follow-up: Repeat liver chemistries.
Observation.
Elastography and labs: ANA, anti-smooth muscle antibody, ceruloplasmin, alpha1-antitrypsin, antigliadin, antiendomysial antibody.

footnotes.footnote: Abbreviations: ERCP, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography; MRCP, magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography.
Adapted from AGA Clinical Practice Committee. AGA medical position statement: evaluation of liver chemistry tests. Gastroenterology 2002;123:1364-1366.

cell.label: Elevated serum bilirubin. Perform history and physical examination. Order liver chemistries.
Unconjugated bilirubin elevated with normal alkaline phosphatase, ALT, AST.
Hemolysis studies, review medications, consider evaluation for Gilbert's disease.
RUQ ultrasound to assess for ductal dilatation.
Refer for ERCP/MRCP.
Evaluation for elevated ALT/AST. Consider AMA, ERCP/MRCP, liver biopsy.

cell.label: Elevated serum alkaline phosphatase
History and physical examination. Liver chemistries
GGT or 5'-nucleotidase
Etiology is not hepatobiliary: Consider bone or placental sources
RUQ ultrasound. Review medications AMA
RUQ ultrasound to assess for ductal dilatation
ERCP/MRCP
AMA
Negative
Evaluation for elevated ALT/AST ERCP/MRCP. Consider liver biopsy
